content.hook: Why should I care about rebalancing if stocks keep going up?
content.bite: Risk drift happens quietly over time. In a multi-asset portfolio, equities grow faster than cash or bonds, subtly turning a moderate investor into an aggressive gambler right before a market dip.
content.analogy: Imagine your portfolio is an RPG squad: 70% Global Equities are your Attack, 30% Bonds/Money Market your Defense. After a big rally your squad drifts to 85% Attack / 15% Defense — riskier than you wanted!
content.takeaway: Rebalancing = selling a bit of what ran hot to replenish what lagged. Disciplined profit-taking without emotional FOMO.

quiz.question: Your equity share spiked from 70% to 85% during a bull market. What does rebalancing do?

options.text: Double down on high-beta tech stocks
options.explanation: That increases risk drift — the opposite of rebalancing. −5 XP.

options.text: Sell 15% of equities to replenish the shield buffer
options.explanation: Sell high on what ran hot, buy the lagged side. +25 XP.

options.text: Panic sell everything into the checking account
options.explanation: Panic selling locks in the rally's risk at the worst timing. −5 XP.

title: The Silent Wealth Killer — what a 1.5% fund fee REALLY costs

content.hook: A 1.5% management fee sounds tiny. What's 1.5 out of 100?
content.bite: Over a 35-year horizon with €200/month at 7% gross: at 0.20% TER (clean ETF) you end with ≈ €335,000 — at 1.80% TER (traditional active bank fund) only ≈ €212,000. The 'innocent' 1.6% delta devours €123,000+, over 36% of your lifetime wealth.

quiz.question: Which TER change has the biggest impact on your wealth over 35 years?

options.text: Lowering TER from 2.5% to 0.2% in an Altersvorsorgedepot
options.explanation: Fee drag compounds: the difference over 35 years can exceed a third of total wealth. +25 XP.
Compounding turns 'rounding noise' into six figures lost. −5 XP.

options.text: Only matters if the ETF underperforms
options.explanation: TER is charged regardless of performance — it compounds in both directions. −5 XP.

content.hook: Is Car Liability legally mandatory but Bicycle Liability isn't — why?
content.legalReality: § 823 BGB: you are personally liable with 100% of current assets AND all future earnings, for life, without limit.

comparison.car: Betriebsgefahr: massive kinetic energy — the state protects third-party victims
comparison.personal: Bikes/pedestrians: lower statistical kinetic energy, no state mandate

comparison.car: Uninsured → the state seizes your license plate immediately
comparison.personal: Bike + phone + ICE crash → €3,000,000+ out of pocket for life

content.takeaway: A €3–5/month Privathaftpflicht is the cheapest anti-ruin shield in the world. Check for modern net-tariff clauses (grobe Fahrlässigkeit, loss of keys).

quiz.question: Why is Kfz-Haftpflicht mandatory by law but Privathaftpflicht isn't?

options.text: Cars carry massive kinetic energy — third-party victims need guaranteed protection
options.explanation: Betriebsgefahr: the state protects victims, not you. Your own cover is voluntary. +25 XP.

options.text: Bicycles can't cause any relevant damage
options.explanation: A bike crash into an ICE train can cost €3M+. −5 XP.

options.text: The law was written before bicycles existed
options.explanation: It's about kinetic energy and victims, not history. −5 XP.

title: The Altersvorsorgedepot Unpacked — why Riester failed, and the depot is different

content.hook: Why did Riester fail, and why is the new depot different?
content.bite: Old Riester plans legally forced a 100% nominal capital guarantee. In a zero-interest era, providers parked money in negative-yielding bonds instead of equities. The new Altersvorsorgedepot drops that restrictive guarantee: 100% global equity compounding, government matching and tax deferral stay.

quiz.question: What made Riester contracts fail young savers during the zero-interest era?

options.text: The legal 100% capital guarantee pushed providers into negative-yielding bonds instead of equities
options.explanation: Guarantee ≈ bonds only ≈ no compounding power for 40 years. +25 XP.
The killer was the guarantee-driven asset allocation, not taxes. −5 XP.

options.text: You could only pay in during December
options.explanation: Contributions work all year — the guarantee is the problem. −5 XP.
